subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose an opt-in `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` setting and core-owned fence for deferred context-engine maintenance, or should this recovery policy instead use an existing generic timeout or plugin-owned contract?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally upgrade-safe by default, but choosing a new public setting and defining when core may release a session before plugin work has unwound is a durable product and compatibility contract that automated review cannot select.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in core contract
options.body: Accept the documented disabled-by-default timeout and fence as the supported way to unblock queued turns, then complete exact-head owner review.

options.title: Use an existing lifecycle contract
options.body: Ask for a narrow rewrite that reuses the chosen generic compaction or runtime timeout path without adding this new operator setting.

options.title: Defer the policy
options.body: Keep the PR open but pause landing until context-engine ownership defines the intended timeout and late-side-effect contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the documented disabled-by-default timeout and fence as the supported way to unblock queued turns, then complete exact-head owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this contributor as the only concrete recent author across the proposed timeout and fence surface; an agents/runtime owner should sponsor the final product decision.
